headline: Gas main work on Fulton Street and Brogan Road approved; Medford High School press release approved; $269,295.81 Law Department funding tabled.
summary: The city also approved a $35,000 consultant for the police chief search and money for three city buildings. The Fire Department's drone program went to committee, and residents spoke about high school costs and speeding on Sturgis Street.
decisions: Approved resolution inviting residents to Mama's free store on November 14 and the winter preparedness event on November 19.
Approved the Public Works and Facilities Committee report on snow plowing and private ways.
Approved National Grid's request for a grant of location to replace about 1,665 feet of gas main on Fulton Street and Brogan Road, 6-0 with one member absent.
Approved deleting zoning section 94-7.5 on vacant and foreclosing properties, effective August 4th, 2027, with one member absent.
Approved resolution requesting an update from the administration on the Veterans Services Department vacancy.
Approved joint press release on next steps for the Medford High School project, 6-0 with one member absent.
Approved resolution asking the administration for a report on the possible sale of Cataldo Ambulance and its contract terms.
Approved $35,000 from the general stabilization fund for the police chief search consultant MGT, with one member absent.
Approved $85,000 and $71,000 from the capital stabilization fund and $24,476.44 from the general stabilization fund for three city buildings, with one member absent.
Tabled the $269,295.81 supplemental appropriation for the Law Department until the next regular meeting.
Referred the Fire Department drone program and surveillance use policy to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.
discussion: High school project cost: Speakers said the project is too expensive and asked for more cuts. Members said a cost impact will come February 2nd, 2027, and listed other funding ideas such as new growth and the pension funding finishing around 2033.

Law Department funding: Members asked whether the $269,295.81 could be set aside another way before the tax classification hearing on November 17. The chief of staff said no feasible way had been found, so the item was tabled.
Police chief search: A member asked for a public meeting with the recruiting firm. The chief of staff said recruitment talks are usually kept out of public meetings.
Sturgis Street speeding: Residents asked for a speed table or removable speed humps and a stop sign at Sturgis and Morgan. Members said they would set up a Saturday site meeting with traffic staff.

Cataldo Ambulance sale: Members asked about a possible sale and ambulances parked in business lots. The company's representative said there is no imminent sale and that ambulances are placed to cover the community.
